name: WebGL2 - ThreeJS Demos
description:
WebGL2 - ThreeJS Demos is a showcase of real-time 3D graphics powered by Three.js and WebGL2, running natively on the Switch browser. It's a curated gallery of sixteen self-contained examples, each built to stress a different advanced rendering technique.

How it works. The home page is a simple gallery of cards — a thumbnail and a short description for each demo. Clicking one opens that example as its own standalone page; there's no streaming or plugins involved, since a full local build of the Three.js engine ships inside the app and every scene renders live on the device's GPU through WebGL2. Together the demos act as a practical proof of what the browser's graphics stack can handle, from GPU-driven simulation and physics to modern post-processing.

What's inside:

  • Geometry & instancing — a textured spinning cube and thousands of individually animated instances drawn efficiently.
  • Lighting & materials — soft-shadowed spotlights with light "cookies", real-time reflective cubemaps, EXR environment maps, and hardware-decoded video mapped onto a grid of cubes.
  • Post-processing — a chunky retro pixelation pass and cinematic Unreal-style bloom.
  • Advanced GPU techniques — a GPU-computed water surface, multiple render targets, uniform buffer objects, layered 2D texture arrays (shown as MRI slices), and a procedural atmospheric sky.
  • Loaders & physics — glTF and Collada 3D model loading, plus a rigid-body scene driven by the Rapier physics engine compiled to WebAssembly.

A great tour of what modern WebGL2 can do on the Switch. Runs offline.
